claims.text: As-cast bulk MnNiSi-based alloys exhibit a large magnetocaloric effect.
As-cast bulk MnNiSi-based alloys are vulnerable to surface-initiated mechanical degradation under cyclic loading.
A thin ductile metallic coating with a graded interlayer will improve the surface mechanical performance of MnNiSi-based alloys.
The coating system will mitigate surface-crack initiation and propagation.
The coating system will not significantly alter the intrinsic magnetocaloric effect.
The proposed ductile metallic coating is approximately 1–3 µm thick and is deposited by physical vapor deposition.
A graded interlayer will enhance coating adhesion.
A graded interlayer can better match the thermal expansion behavior of the coating and MnNiSi-based substrate.
Depositing the coating below 200 °C will have minimal thermal impact on the bulk phase transformation responsible for the magnetocaloric effect.
A well-adhered multilayer coating will smooth or cover surface flaws.
A well-adhered multilayer coating will distribute applied mechanical stress more evenly.
The ductile coating will absorb and redistribute cyclic stresses.
Absorption and redistribution of cyclic stresses will delay surface-crack initiation and propagation.
Accommodation of thermal-expansion differences by the graded interlayer will reduce interfacial stress and help preserve the bulk magnetocaloric phase transition.
Coated samples will have greater wear resistance than uncoated as-cast samples.
Coated samples will have longer fatigue lives than uncoated as-cast samples.
The magnetocaloric entropy change of coated samples will remain within approximately 10% of that of the uncoated baseline.
The proposed enhancement should hold under cyclic loading at operating temperatures below approximately 200 °C.
Excessively high operating temperatures or extreme environmental conditions may compromise coating integrity.
